target_customer: Startups and recruiting agencies screening technical candidates; the current site also targets high-volume frontline hiring
problem: Technical screens consume engineering time and are vulnerable to cheating. Lightscreen runs a voice and video AI interviewer with cheating detection and rubric-based evaluations.
business_model: B2B SaaS for AI interviewing and hiring workflows (pricing not found)

founders.name: Gavin Saldanha
founders.background_notes: From the YC page: ML and NLP background, led engineering teams at Cauzal AI and Stacked, co-authored a text generation paper with IBM Watson.

founders.name: Prachie Banthia
founders.background_notes: From the YC page: helped sell RideOS to GoPuff for 115M USD. Role at Lightscreen and education not listed. The founders met at Google.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time voice and video interviewing with interruption handling and multi-modal cheating detection is demanding, but by 2024 built on commodity speech and LLM APIs; founders include a former AssemblyAI product lead.

defensibility.rationale: Voice interviewer products are copyable on shared model APIs and the market drew several rivals; no data or network moat is evident.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Sources found describe AI interviewers from micro1, HeyMilo, Mercor and HackerEarth but give no launch dates near the batch, so the timing of competition is unverified.

market_need_then: Technical screening is a recurring engineering time cost and the company cites cheating as a problem; no spend or customer-count data from 2024 was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses lightscreen.ai; legal entity is Lightscreen Inc (BuiltWith).

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, product focused with plain-English workflow claims

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand found; name is generic and shared with an unrelated LightScreen flashlight tool.

pivots.from: Voice and video AI interviewer for technical screening
pivots.to: End-to-end AI recruiting pipeline, including frontline hiring
pivots.why: Not stated; current site lists a five-stage hiring pipeline and a separate tech hiring page

outcome_analysis: Lightscreen began in 2024 as a voice and video technical interviewer and by 2026 its site describes a broader hiring pipeline with 20 plus customers (vendor-claimed). Only aggregator funding data exists (about 500K USD around December 2024), the team is small, and no exit or shutdown appeared. Many AI interview rivals make its outcome unclear.
notes: Aggregators (VCBacked, Extruct, FundedIQ, PitchBook) report about 500K USD seed around 2024-12 with Y Combinator and Rebel Fund, not confirmed by a primary source, so not recorded as a round. Competitor search found AI interviewer rivals but no dated launches near Fall 2024, so the list is empty. Headcount differs (YC 2, PitchBook 3). Pivot inferred from comparing the YC description with the current website; timing unknown.
